## What does a row mean?

[Scooter and Bike Availability 2024](https://opendata.minneapolismn.gov/datasets/c9e75387ca8343ab8a68a4f3446cd9bc_0/explore)
contains hourly availability snapshots. Each record reports `NumberAvailable`
for a company, poll time, closest street or trail segment, and neighborhood.
We will check whether those fields uniquely identify records below.

These are availability counts, not trips or unique vehicle counts. A vehicle
can appear in many consecutive snapshots. The table has no coordinates or
geometry: `ClosestCenterlineID` is a join key for a separate street/trail dataset.
The city notes that some centerline information is withheld for privacy or is
unrecorded for certain vehicle statuses. Missing locations are not zero availability.

For a manageable first look, we use **July 15, 2024, midnight to midnight in
America/Chicago**. This is a deliberately selected day, not a representative
sample of the year. Download it from the repository root with
`python3 analysis/download_availability.py`. All summaries and plots below use
this one day unless explicitly labeled otherwise.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(jsonlite)

# Support execution from either the analysis directory or repository root.
root <- if (file.exists("data/availability_metadata.json")) "." else ".."
meta <- fromJSON(file.path(root, "data/availability_metadata.json"))
raw <- read_csv(file.path(root, "data/availability_2024-07-15.csv"),
                col_types = cols(
                  PollTime = col_double(), CompanyName = col_character(),
                  NumberAvailable = col_double(), ClosestCenterlineID = col_character(),
                  ClosestCenterlineType = col_character(), Neighborhood = col_character(),
                  ObjectId = col_double()
                ))
stopifnot(nrow(raw) == meta$subset_rows, !anyDuplicated(raw$ObjectId))

# ArcGIS dates are milliseconds since the Unix epoch; the service declares UTC.
availability <- raw |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ na_if(na_if(trimws(.x), ""), "NULL")),
         poll_time = as.POSIXct(PollTime / 1000, origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"),
         local_hour = as.integer(format(poll_time, tz = "America/Chicago", format = "%H")))

tibble(scope = c("Full service", "Selected local day"),
       rows = c(meta$full_dataset_rows, nrow(raw)))
glimpse(availability)
```

## Fields, missing values, and coverage

```{r}
# Retain centerline IDs as text, even when they look numeric.
meta$schema$fields |> select(name, type, nullable) |> knitr::kable()

tibble(variable = names(raw),
       missing = vapply(availability[names(raw)], function(x) sum(is.na(x)), integer(1)),
       percent_missing = round(100 * missing / nrow(raw), 2)) |>
  knitr::kable()

availability |>
  summarise(first_poll_utc = min(poll_time), last_poll_utc = max(poll_time),
            distinct_poll_times = n_distinct(poll_time),
            companies = n_distinct(CompanyName, na.rm = TRUE),
            neighborhoods = n_distinct(Neighborhood, na.rm = TRUE),
            negative_counts = sum(NumberAvailable < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            zero_counts = sum(NumberAvailable == 0, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  knitr::kable()

summary(availability$NumberAvailable)
availability |> count(CompanyName, name = "records", sort = TRUE)
availability |> count(ClosestCenterlineType, name = "records", sort = TRUE)

# Inspect repeated candidate keys before assuming one row per segment/poll.
duplicate_keys <- availability |>
  count(PollTime, CompanyName, ClosestCenterlineID, ClosestCenterlineType,
        Neighborhood, name = "records") |>
  filter(records > 1)
tibble(repeated_candidate_keys = nrow(duplicate_keys),
       records_in_repeated_keys = sum(duplicate_keys$records))
head(duplicate_keys, 10)
```

On this selected day, `r sum(is.na(availability$ClosestCenterlineID))`
records (`r round(100 * mean(is.na(availability$ClosestCenterlineID)), 1)`%)
have no centerline ID after converting literal `"NULL"` values to missing.
These records would need explicit accounting in a later map.

## How large are individual reported counts?

```{r}
#| label: fig-count-distribution
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of counts per record on the selected day."
ggplot(availability, aes(NumberAvailable)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, boundary = -0.5, fill = "#247B91", color = "white") +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = "log1p") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of reported availability per record",
       subtitle = "July 15, 2024",
       x = "Available vehicles per record", y = "Records (log1p scale)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Exactly `r round(100 * mean(availability$NumberAvailable == 3), 1)`% of
records report **3** available vehicles. That concentration is worth investigating;
the field documentation does not explain it, so we should not assume a cause.
The maximum is `r max(availability$NumberAvailable)` vehicles in one record,
which could warrant inspecting the associated segment before mapping it.

## How does recorded availability change over the day?

```{r}
# Sum within a poll and company, never across hours to estimate unique vehicles.
# Preserve a missing total if any contributing count is unknown.
by_poll <- availability |>
  group_by(poll_time, CompanyName) |>
  summarise(available = if (anyNA(NumberAvailable)) NA_real_ else sum(NumberAvailable),
            records = n(), .groups = "drop")

by_poll |> group_by(CompanyName) |>
  summarise(observed_polls = n(), min_rows_per_poll = min(records),
            max_rows_per_poll = max(records), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable()

# Points avoid implying continuous observation between polls or across gaps.
ggplot(by_poll, aes(poll_time, available, color = CompanyName)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_datetime(timezone = "America/Chicago", date_labels = "%H:%M", date_breaks = "4 hours") +
  labs(title = "Recorded availability at each poll, by company",
       subtitle = "July 15, 2024; changes can reflect reporting as well as actual availability",
       x = "Minneapolis local time", y = "Sum of reported available vehicles", color = "Company") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Questions to investigate next

- Are polls present at every expected hour for each company? Missing polls
  should remain missing, rather than being replaced by zero.
- Do company patterns persist across other days and seasons?
- How often is the centerline ID missing, and does that vary by company?
- After joining the matching street and trail geometry, where is availability
  concentrated? A missing segment record does not establish zero availability.

There is no separate vehicle-type field, although company labels include
"Lime Bikes" and "Veo Bikes". Availability alone cannot measure ridership,
demand, or equitable access. Neighborhood
comparisons would also need a justified denominator and reporting-coverage checks.
